disclaimer: 21+ adults only. Educational geography and plant-type talk — not medical advice, not a grow guide, not a live menu. Bag art is concept mockups only.
bagsDisclaimer: Four packaging mockups with flower stills — not inventory, not for sale, no prices, no license on the pouch. Indoor vs outdoor talk is shopper education (consistency vs sun and place), not how to grow.

bags.name: Ridge Satchel
bags.story: A small flap satchel mockup for the everyday jar story. This is a drawing of a bag, not a SKU. Indoor lots are the shop talk about even color and a calendar that does not wait on summer.
bags.cultivationNote: Indoor, in this mockup, means room-grown under electric light: tighter, more repeatable-looking flower in the jar. We are not listing watts, nutrients, or a recipe.

bags.name: Trail Satchel
bags.story: Same satchel shape, sun-grown art. Outdoor flower follows season, hillside, and night swing — more place in the jar, more variation from lot to lot.
bags.cultivationNote: Outdoor here is the sun-and-season story: full-spectrum light and altitude show up as character. Still a mockup. Still not a grow guide.

bags.name: Clinic Pouch
bags.story: A labeled medicinal-style pouch — concept only. No dose, no claim, no live menu. Indoor indica on the art is a type-and-room story, not a prescription.
bags.cultivationNote: Indoor rooms keep climate off the weather map, so shoppers often hear about consistency. After harvest, shops talk about cure — we do not give times or temps.

bags.name: Summit Pouch
bags.story: Same medical pouch idea, highland outdoor art. Broad-leaf mountain nights on the label, still a mockup, still not medicine in a bag.
bags.cultivationNote: Outdoor indica talk on this card is terroir and short highland seasons — culture and botany. Call a clinician for health questions. Do not treat this pouch as product on a shelf.

types.name: Indica
types.history: The word indica has been used for short, broad-leaf plants tied to highland Central Asia. Think resin-rich mountain populations and short seasons — culture and botany, not a dosing chart.
types.originNote: Classic pins sit on the Hindu Kush range and northern Afghanistan.

types.name: Sativa
types.history: Sativa, in shop talk, usually means taller, narrower-leaf expressions from warmer latitudes. Names like Thai, Durban, Colombian, Mexican, Jamaican, and Acapulco Gold are trade and landrace stories — not grow recipes.
types.originNote: Pins run from Southeast Asia to southern Africa, the Caribbean, and highland Mexico.

types.name: Hybrid
types.history: Most modern shop flower is a hybrid of older regional lines. The Indian subcontinent, for example, holds a long cultural record that spans fiber, ritual, and mixed highland expressions — a reminder that types blur at the edges.
types.originNote: See hybrid-landrace pins on the Origins map — educational geography only.

types.name: Hemp
types.history: Hemp is the fiber-and-seed side of the cannabis story. East Asia — especially the Yellow River basin — has deep archaeological and historical records of hemp for cloth, seed, and ceremony.
types.originNote: Not a high-THC shop type. History of use, not a grow guide.

types.name: Ruderalis
types.history: C. ruderalis is tied to short-season northern latitudes — roadside and steppe habitats across southern Russia and east-central Europe. Breeders later borrowed the day-neutral habit. We talk history, not how to breed.
types.originNote: The Origins map marks the ruderalis belt as geography, not a product list.
